featured_reviews.name: Sadhana Viswanadhuni
featured_reviews.review_text:
As a true Hyderabadi my search for such amazing biryani never ends! I hated mumbai for not having it here! But now I don't need to look any further😍😍😍
Biryani By Kilo's biryani are sooo hyderabadi in taste that one is definitely going to have a foodgasm!❤️
My search ends here today as now I'm gonna keep ordering from BBK to satisfy my biryani cravings 😍😍 We ordered for
Paneer Nawabi Curry ✨
A delectable paneer dish! The gravy was very smooth with the right amount of spices and softtt paneer 😍
Ulte Tawa ka Parantha ✨
It's like a thicker smaller version of rumali roti but much better than that! As we ordered the food earlier we heated it up on tawa and savoured it with the paneer curry 😍
Veg Hyderabadi Biryani ✨
A properly packed flavoured rice with amazingly marinated veggies! The masalas were right and yummm. What more?? They even serve it with SALAN like in Hyderabad!!!!! 😍😍😍💞
Veg Kathal Dum Biryani ✨ - MUST HAVE!!!!!!!
This delicacy of south is a seasonal favourite and I was very doubtful if it would match to my expectations and mind me it was way beyond that! It had the perfect taste like we get it back in south!
And it was a super hit with all my family members!
😍😍😍
The biryanis were served with
Onion and lemon salad
Salan and Raita too❤️

Coming to the packaging can you think of any other better eco friendly packaging?? To top it off they even provided us with an aanch lighting which allows one to place the pot on candle burner! Which is sure to keep the handi and rice in it warm and fresh😍😍😍

If the green dough sealing gets hard and tough to remove! Don't hesitate to take help of a knife! That part might be tricky but I think a good sealed bowl is very important for perfect biryani 😍🤤🤤

So happy to have stumbled upon this brand! Forever thankful for bringing Hyderabadi Biryani to Mumbai 😍😍😍😍😍😍😍

featured_reviews.name: Rajat Sharma
featured_reviews.review_text:
Biryani by Kilo is one of safest and trusted brand delivering quality biryanis to our doorstep.
Last Thursday we ordered some of the dishes from there. The best thing about them was they deliver biryanis in earthen pots.
Delivery was quick and on time.
The dishes we tried were :

1) Hyderabadi Chicken Biryani (5/5) : Served in a earthen pot with live heating candles. The rice was cooked well. Chicken pieces were perfectly coojed in spices. Overall the biryani was awesome.
Salan and raita was complementary with the biryani was so good.

2) Chicken Korma (5/5) : It was lil sweet as I love. Chicken cooked in thick gravy had lipsmacking flavours. It was also packed in earthern pot.

3) Ulte Tawa ka Paratha (5/5) : It was just perfect. I was trying this first time and really love it.

All the dishes were scrumptious and enough for 3 people .
Hygine and stromg packing was done to avoid spillage and contamination.
Proper safety checks were done.

They made my day, surely gonna order them again.

featured_reviews.review_text: Are you a biryani lover ? If yes then Biryani by kilo is what you should try must. Very impressed with their matka packing which is being offered with candle and a mud pot to heat thir biryani before having it. Secondly packing was excellent and food delivered was peeping hot. Also there is a chutney served along with biryani which is a perfect combination to have with their biryani. Paneer nawabi was good in taste specially the paneer pieces were very soft. Overall a good first experience with them. Will surely try their other varieties in Biryani specially.

featured_reviews.name: Priyanka Kwatra
featured_reviews.review_text:
Best Biryani ever! I love Biryani by Kilo. They have the longest, most flavourful rice in their Biryani. We love their Hyderabadi Biryani the most. It is spicy and made in masalas. It comes with delicious salan, onions and green chutney. The chicken in the biryani is nice and juicy and quantity is also quite good. The handi has to be heated for 5-7 mins before having it. It is Highly recommended to do so as it gives steamy hot well done rice in your plate and it feels we are at a restaurant.
We also had chicken korma with ulta tawa parathas. Korma was also delicious and had quite authentic taste and flavor. The paratha when heated on tawa became nice and flaky. Suggest you to do the same but not too much as it becomes too crisp.
Overall Excellent food delivery and always trustworthy for the taste and flavor. Value for money!

featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently visited Veranda around 4 PM, and the first thing to note is that the kitchen was partially closed at that time, which limited a few options. Still, we managed to order a decent variety of dishes.
We tried prawns thecha, chicken 65, chicken tenders, pizza, pasta, and Hakka noodles. Most of the food was actually good and enjoyable. The highlight of the meal was definitely the prawns thecha, easily the best dish on the table. It was flavorful, well-cooked, and something I’d genuinely go back for.
The pizza and pasta were nice, chicken 65 was solid, and overall the food quality was pretty satisfying. But the Hakka noodles were a letdown. They had a strong smell, likely from the egg and chicken, which made it hard to enjoy the dish.
Another downside was the timing of the chicken tenders. They arrived way too late, almost after we were done eating everything else, which kind of ruined the flow of the meal.
That said, the ambience is where Veranda really stands out. The place looks amazing, has a great vibe, and the location is perfect for a chill outing in Bandra.
Overall, it’s a good place with great ambience and mostly good food, but a few issues with timing and consistency in dishes hold it back slightly.

featured_reviews.name: Supreet Kini
featured_reviews.review_text:
A friend's scouring of places and suggestions bought us to the Good Luck Restaurant, in Bandra. It is situated right next to Mehboob Studio, at a busy junction in Bandra. The place is more known for it's breakfast dishes, and is usually crowded.

The ambience is vintage, takes you back to the old Bombay nostalgia, and the menu is typically Parsi. They have a small convenience store as well.

The food is a mix of typical Bombay Parsi and middle eastern. We were pretty hungry, and started off with a bunch of pavs and kheema fry beef. Served piping hot, the crunchy pavs go wonderfully well with the spicy beef kheema. Next we ordered, the kheema ghotala beef, which had more of an egg consistency. I personally liked the kheema fry more than the kheema ghotala. Next up was the lovely chicken shawarma, with generous amounts of chicken and mayo.

The flagship dish of this place is the bun maska accompanied by Irani chai which soon followed suit. A few mutton samosas later, we ordered the final dish of the day - more crunchy pavs with Chicken Handi, upon the recommendation of the waiter. It was a tad bit disappointing compared to the earlier dishes.

Overall, the food gets a healthy rating of 4/5, the vintage ambience another 4/5. Service was pretty fast as we were one of only 3 tables at 8PM on a Friday evening. A great visit if you're in the area, and are looking for a filling meal at a reasonable price.

Title: A Flavourful Journey at FRENY – ALL DAY DINING & BAR: A Must-Visit Experience

Prepare to embark on a journey through the flavours of East India, as each dish on the menu showcases the region's rich culinary heritage. The Masala Tiger Prawns are a true delight, bursting with flavour and sure to tantalize your taste buds. For those craving something with a bit of a kick, the Chicken Wings and Chicken Indyal Tacos are mind-bogglingly delicious, offering a perfect balance of spice and savoury goodness.

However, the true highlight of the meal is the desserts. The Jardin Du Rose and Fernandes Rocher are not only exquisitely presented but also deliver on taste and flavour. In conclusion, FRENY – ALL DAY DINING & BAR is more than just a place to eat—it's an experience that must be savoured. With its inviting ambiance, exceptional service, and unforgettable flavours, it's a culinary journey you won't want to miss. Make sure to add it to your list of must-visit destinations.

featured_reviews.name: Anil Avinash Kaushik
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited Freny’s All Day Dining & Bar and absolutely loved the food and vibe.

Starters:

Bottle Masala Chicken Wings – flavourful and well cooked

Masala Tiger Prawns – delicious and packed with spice

They also served complimentary Fugiyas, which were soft, fresh, and a great start to the meal.(Loved the chutney 100/100)

Mains:

Tried both the Prawns Thali and Fish Thali, and they were outstanding.
Each thali included:

- Puris curry

- Rava fried prawns / rava fried surmai

- Bombil tel kanda

- East Indian green dal

- Fugiyas

- Rice, rotya, and wedding pickle

Everything tasted authentic, comforting, and perfectly balanced truly a highlight of the meal.

Mocktails:

B’ananas (espresso shot with banana & pineapple juice) – unfortunately didn’t work for me at all. I’m a coffee lover, but this combination didn’t go well.

Tangerine Spritz (non-alcoholic Aperol-style spritz with rosemary) – refreshing and decent, though not exceptional.

Service:
The staff member who took our order was knowledgeable about the menu, which was appreciated. There was some confusion during billing,  we were advised to use Zomato for payment, but weren’t properly guided through the process. However, this felt like a minor issue.

Overall, excellent food, great vibe, and a lovely place for authentic coastal/East Indian cuisine. Minor service hiccups aside, definitely worth visiting and I’d happily return.

featured_reviews.name: amin shaikh
featured_reviews.review_text:
We recently visited Freny’s All Day Dining Bar on Linking Road, Bandra West, and absolutely loved the experience! The space is warm, inviting, and thoughtfully designed — it truly feels like walking into someone’s charming East Indian home.
The interiors are a beautiful blend of retro, European, Portuguese, and East Indian décor — from pastel colors and vintage chandeliers to framed family photos and wallpapered ceilings. The ground floor gives off cosy café vibes, while the upper floor offers a more formal dining space with a well-stocked bar and nostalgic touches throughout. Every corner tells a story!
We tried a variety of items and everything was delicious:
Mocktails: Chocolate Skyline, Boozy Bougie Pop, Rose Ciel – all refreshing and unique!
Desserts: Tiramisu Dreamin, Caramel Apple, Cheese Basque Cake, Jardin Du Rose, and the star of the show — Matilda’s Chocolate Cake. Rich, moist, and absolutely unforgettable — hands down one of the best cakes we’ve had!
They also serve traditional East Indian dishes like fugiyas, alongside modern café-style fare including pizzas, burgers, and salads — offering something for everyone.
If you’re in Bandra, Freny’s is a must-visit spot for its heartwarming ambiance, nostalgic charm, and standout food & drinks. Can’t wait to go

We were served with two fugiyas and chutney butter along with it as a welcome snacks which were both delicious.We visited this place for dinner unfortunately were not able to get what we wanted from the menu. Wanted the mac and cheese balls which were not available and neither were the sweet potato fries and other regular fries with bottle masala.

We finally ordered the fried chicken reccomended which was awful, the chicken seemed frozen and tasteless, like it has been kept for long before frying. The zucchini fries were recommended to us but was just about ok no taste or flavour but a good portion the batter covering was too thick, served along with sauce.

The thali had a rice bowl portion, a tasty yellow prawn curry, a delicious green dal, lovely wedding pickle, the dry bombil was an added accompaniment and fugiyas along with a few fried prawns. Sharing good food is a love language, so if you’re in Mumbai (or traveling from there), you have to try this. I’m definitely ordering this for my friends!

This place by the Bawa Hotels Group is a good option if you’re in the mood for Punjabi food, just don’t walk in expecting completely authentic flavours. The taste is slightly toned down, but if you set your expectations right, you’ll actually enjoy the food.

The menu is quite well done, and the meal box options are a big plus. Makes ordering super easy without having to overthink or pick too many individual items.

Their parathas are definitely worth trying—served nicely with curd. Do ask for white butter separately though, as it’s not given by default and really makes a difference. The lassi is a must-have here, easily one of the better things on the menu.

Also, a special mention for the Kalimiri chicken shorba. It’s not on the menu, but if they have it, don’t miss it—it’s genuinely very good.

Ambience is nice and comfortable, so no complaints there. Service, however, is quite slow and needs serious improvement, which can get a bit frustrating.

Parking is another issue—since it’s close to the railway station, the area is always crowded and finding a spot is tough. Better to plan that in advance.

Overall, a good place to chill and enjoy a meal, as long as you’re okay overlooking the service and parking hassles.

featured_reviews.name: Suhani Mendonsa
featured_reviews.review_text:
Khar just got a delicious new reason to celebrate with Bawa Kitchen opening its doors this Lohri! From the first bite, it felt like a true Punjabi feast — rich, soulful and full of festive warmth. My absolute favourites were their creamy butter chicken, soft and flavourful chhole kulcha, and the super refreshing lassi that perfectly balanced the spices. Every dish tasted like it was made with love and tradition. If you’re craving authentic Punjabi flavours with a celebratory twist, this is the place to be — go check it out and treat yourself to a hearty, happy meal!
And yes, my festive Lohri fit was specially curated — can’t wait to share it with you all soon!

featured_reviews.name: Susheel Dharmani
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited Bawa Kitchen and had a good dining experience overall. The place has a simple yet comfortable ambience, perfect for a relaxed meal.
The food quality was nice, especially the North Indian dishes which were flavorful and well-prepared. Portion sizes were decent and prices felt reasonable for the location.
Service was quick and the staff was polite and attentive. It’s a convenient option if you’re staying nearby or looking for a reliable place to eat in Dadar.
Overall, a good spot for a casual meal with consistent quality.

featured_reviews.name: Jawahar Hingorani
featured_reviews.review_text:
I only gave 4 for atmosphere because there was no 4.5 or 4.75…and I got bitten by mosquitoes! The food was on point - I ordered Ajwaini Rawas for my appetizer and it came with this spicy tandoori salad (think Thai Som Yum but not as sweet or wet) and Green chutney which was the perfect accompaniment. For my mains I got the Mutton Beliram (don’t why it’s called that) which was nice and spicy, along with a roomali roti. I’d recommend ordering a naan instead - lots of very moorish sauce to lap up! Got some Jal Jeera with soda to wash it down (not sure about the boondi). Finished off with some Gulabjamun - there is definitely a hint of “Gulab” there! And just look at those soft, pillowy, inviting mounds. 😆

Overall Bawa Kitchen echoes the punjabi ethos when it comes to food. It’s definitely a place I’d recommend and visit again!

featured_reviews.name: Vijita Sonawane
featured_reviews.review_text: The Bawa Kitchen delivered a great dining experience—pure Punjabi vibes, full balle-balle. The ambience is lively and authentic, with vibrant cut-outs and the iconic “Khatiya” as a standout photo spot. Veg and non-veg starters are well curated and set the right tone for the meal. Special mention to Rahul for being an excellent host—his food suggestions and positive approach added real value to the experience. Overall, a visit that is absolutely worth it for good food, warm hospitality, and Punjabi flair.

featured_reviews.name: Noor Sayeed Khan
featured_reviews.review_text:
Madras Diaries in Bandra has such a gorgeous, welcoming vibe, it’s easily one of the prettiest spots for South Indian food in the city. The staff was genuinely sweet and the service was so smooth it made the whole experience feel really relaxed.

We decided to try their new chaat menu, and the Shakkarkand Matar ki Chaat was a total winner, it felt super fresh and not at all oily. The Chatpata Singhada (water chestnut) was a fun surprise too, especially for that unique crunch you don't usually find in street food.

The Madras Diaries Special Combo is a solid choice if you’re like me and can't decide the medu vada was perfectly crispy. But honestly, the real highlight was the Filter Coffee with those Rawa Biscuits. It’s such a nostalgic, comforting pairing. We finished with the Elaneer Payasum, which was light and refreshing, though I wish there was just a bit more of it! Definitely worth a visit if you’re in Bandra and want a meal that feels both clean and satisfying.

featured_reviews.name: Allen Samuel
featured_reviews.review_text:
Madras Diaries is a perfect blend of authentic South Indian comfort and exciting new flavours! The highlight now is their chaat menu, which adds a fun, chatpata twist alongside their classic offerings.

The Chatpata Singhada and Shakkarkand Matar Ki Chaat were vibrant, tangy, and full of flavour. The Chettinad Paneer with flaky wheat parotta was rich and satisfying, paired beautifully with the soft Kodumai (wheat) parotta. Refreshing sips like the Cold Coffee and Virgin Mojito balanced the meal, while the Elaneer Payasam was a light, delicious finish.

The presentation of each dish was impressive and clearly made with attention to detail. Service was warm and prompt, making the overall experience even more enjoyable.

With its warm décor and relaxed, inviting ambience, Madras Diaries is a must-visit for a wholesome meal with a unique chaat twist!

featured_reviews.name: Aaniket R Naddkarni
featured_reviews.review_text:
VARUGA VARUGA ❤️

Everyone is craving South Indian food these days… looks like Idli & Dosa have officially become Gen Z’s favorite comfort food 😍
So we decided to check out Madras Diaries in Bandra — a place already famous for authentic South Indian food, but now they’ve also launched CHATS… and trust me, this will make you visit again & again!

Without wasting any time, we started with our favorite — Pani Puri 🤤
And bhai sahab… they served it with 3 different flavor waters — Mumbai style, Delhiwala & Kolkata style!
We literally couldn’t stop eating 😅

Then came the Palak Patta Chaat…
And bhai, ekdum Delhi ki yaad dila di ❤️

To beat the summer heat, we tried their Kokum Cooler & Mint Cooler — super refreshing and fresh!

For mains, we ordered Mini Idlies served with 4 different chutneys… and trust me, this combo is something you’ll only get here, so make sure it’s on your order list ✔️

We also tried the Malabar Paratha with Chettinad Paneer — great quantity, rich flavors, and the paneer was super soft 😍

And finally in desserts, Pineapple Sheera… simple, comforting, and honestly made with love ❤️
So make sure you visit Madras Diaries

featured_reviews.name: A P
featured_reviews.review_text: We had lunch at Khane Khas at Bandra west today. First thing I noticed is that the owner Mr Chaddha gave me a warm smile as soon we entered. We started off with Aam panna- made fresh by Mr Chaddha’s mother who is 85 years of age. Perfect taste and quite refreshing. We started with MUTTON SEEKH ROLL. Juicy & tasty mutton kebab in a roll. (5/5). Then we had PUNJABI MUTTON SUKKA ( thick gravy with tender flavorful pieces of mutton - the spices were underplayed perfectly to enhance the flavor of mutton, exactly how I like it) - 5/5. featured_reviews.review_text: This place had hands down the best service I have experienced in Mumbai. In addition to the great food, the plates were spotless, the serving of lachha pyaaz was generous, the water was served a perfect cold and the waiting staff was attentive and prompt. These things don't happen on their own without someone's attention to detail. Incredibly lucky to have dined at a place run so passionately.

featured_reviews.name: akshat singh
featured_reviews.review_text:
Quite a decent restaurant to try out good north indian food. Their spice levels are good and the masala's are used in just the right quantity making the dishes delectable and sumptuous. Their tandoori is absolutely heart-warming but the dhuan chicken was not worth the hype it has.

Ambience is not too great but on a cool windy day, it's a good place. The staff is really polite and helpful. Worth a try outlet for sure.

featured_reviews.name: Ramsha Tausalkar
featured_reviews.review_text: There’s a spot in Bandra that serves North Indian food so good, you’ll forget that you’re in Mumbai and be transported straight to Punjab. It’s called Papa Pancho Da Dhaba and they’ve got a menu that’s small and straightforward - but they do these dishes so well and in such an authentic manner - we for sure haven’t had such North Indian food in Mumbai. The Dal Makhani, Cheese Kulcha, Makhani Chicken, Kasturi Kebab, Dahi Papdi Chaat and Matka Kulfi - all of your seemingly regular dishes but here it’s all elevated, rich and very real. The interiors are colourful and very dhaba-like. If this is a cuisine you enjoy, save this spot!

featured_reviews.name: Dr. Kartik Patil
featured_reviews.review_text:
Papa Pancho da dhaba is a kind of experience amidst the by-lanes of hype Bandra Pali Hill. You get into this colourful world of roadside dhabas as soon as you step in. Sparkly danglers, colourful patakas, slogans written on trucks decorated on the walls.
Food:
Good, guilty and gluttonous North Indian food is served with love on brass cutlery. You feel the butter in every bite. Quality is great, though quantity is frequently insufficient for a couple of people. Earlier they used to include dal makhani and dahi etc. with their mouthwatering kulchas and parathas but now they have stopped doing that. Tandoori Starters and tandoor breads are must try for.
Service: servers are frank and friendly and a bit too nosy sometimes.
Ambience: small place, but they made max out of it. They transfer you to dhaba instantly.
Value for money: This would disappoint you, as for what they ask for; their quantity is too little. Hope they work on their quantity.
A highly recommended place for small group or family to visit if you are craving some good Kulchas, Parathas, Tandooris and a glass full of lassi.

featured_reviews.name: Rivha Dalvi

Imagine a dhaba in the middle of the city and that too in Bandra!! Well got an opportunity to visit “ Papa Pancho da Dhaba” with family. Was surprised on a Thursday night, it was crowded with people waiting to be seated, that is how popular the place is.

We ordered the Tandoori Chicken which was crisp from outside and moist from inside, well spiced and really tasty.  Next was Dahi Pappi Chat, a well balanced crispy, chatpata, khatta meetha, but for the cost, the quantity could be a lil more.

In main course it was Chicken Handi with Butter Garlic Naan, served with Dal Makhni and Curd. Next was but for sure Amritsari Kulcha…. served with white butter dollop and buttery dal makhni. We were almost full, but on suggestion we ordered Chicken Dal Khichadi, which surprisingly was very comforting with bits of Chicken … we ended the meal with  Lassi… a must at any Punjabi place. A huge copper glass full!!

featured_reviews.name: Abhijeet Mukherjee
featured_reviews.review_text: Only a few times in our lives does such a moment occur when a morsel of food touches your tongue and the world immediately comes to a standstill. The chatter in your mind stops and, to your surprise, it asks you to focus on the present. The mind is surprised too, for it seldom finds reality so interesting that it chooses to shutdown the jibber jabber it bombards you with all day. When I sliced into their gooey, hot Carrot Cream Cheese Blondie with my usual lack of care and shoved it into my mouth, this was that moment for me.  And then came the coffee. And then the breakfast next day. The food, the prices (why are all other places ripping us off!) and the oldies rock in the background … what’s not to love!

I’m so glad we came across this place! by far one of the best in Bandra right now.
We tried a couple of their snacks, but the standout was definitely the chicken croissant. It was absolutely amazing, flaky, buttery, and packed with flavor. I’ve had chicken croissants from several high end places, but this one genuinely holds its own and, in many cases, tastes better.
What really makes the experience even better is the pricing! it’s very reasonable for the quality you’re getting, which makes it feel like great value overall.
The staff are also incredibly nice and welcoming. They speak so politely and create such a warm, homely atmosphere that you immediately feel comfortable.
Overall, a fantastic find with great food, great value, and genuinely lovely service. Easily a new favorite spot. Highly recommend Joseph’s Table !

featured_reviews.review_text:
Family Table is a great meat snack house in Bandra. Best to take away your meal as they have limited outdoor seating.

I've tried a bunch of options over the years and have never been disappointed (so long as your expectations are aligned and you know what you're here for). Don't expect full-fledged restaurant type service or *perfectly* spiced potatoes - this one knows its audience and caters to it well. They've got bacon quiches, shephards pie, boat-type flatbreads, pattices, rolls, cutlets, and the usual snacks that will keep you coming back. If you're craving fugiyas, this should be your go-to; they sell it by the dozen. Pop those baddies in an air fryer for some added crisp, and you've got the perfect bread to sop up gravies or pair with dips. I even do them with my favourite marmalade as a breakfast snack sometimes.

They also have heavier meal options like the cafreal roast with mash/veggies, stuffed meat poies with wedges, and filling burgers. The foods not always a 100% authentic, but usually quite satisfying. I've never tried their biryanis and rice dishes but those are available too. Everything is also quite reasonably priced for a premium bandra location.

Thanks for serving, family style 🤘. Reminds me of simpler times when getting a good meal didn't require you to shell out big money.

featured_reviews.name: Benjamin SHIH
featured_reviews.review_text:
This is my first time visiting India, and I’m so glad we found this gem. The Owner/Chef is incredibly welcoming; he personally helped us order and explained the flavors with such passion.
We are from Taiwan and have tried many top-tier Indian restaurants back home, like Saffron (番紅花), Taj (泰姬), and Mayur (馬友友). But the Gosht Lucknowi Dum Biryani here is on a whole different level. My friend even said it’s 10 times better!
• The Mutton: I’ve never had mutton this tender. It’s perfectly marinated and practically falls apart. You can really taste the "Kung Fu" the Chef puts into the slow-cooking.
• The Sauce: That rich, golden gravy isn't just a sauce; it's a concentration of slow-cooked onions and spices that melt in your mouth.
• The Pro Move: Make sure to mix in the spicy yogurt raita. It cuts through the richness and adds a whole new layer of flavor to the fragrant rice.
If you want a meal made with genuine heart and soul, this is the place. A huge thank you to the Chef for such a warm welcome to India!

featured_reviews.name: Shreeya Mehrotra
featured_reviews.review_text:
I’m a North Indian living in Mumbai, and everyone knows that Mumbai doesn’t really do good North Indian food unless it’s fancy. Most days you just adjust, but some days you really miss proper food. That’s exactly the kind of day I found Bombay Curry and honestly I’m so glad I did. This place feels so homely. It’s the kind of place you go to on a random night when you’ve had a bad day, you’re tired and you just want something that feels like home.

We ordered butter chicken, garlic naan and seekh kebab and every single thing was a straight 10/10. The butter chicken was rich and comforting, the garlic naan was soft and perfect and the seekh kebabs were juicy and full of flavour.

What makes it even more special is knowing that the chefs are from Lucknow and Rajasthan because you can genuinely taste that authenticity in the food. And the chef/owner himself was easily one of the most friendly and nicest chefs I’ve ever met. Warm, welcoming and clearly cooking with a lot of love. Bombay Curry feels like a hug on a plate.

featured_reviews.name: Sagar “Sagar Anil” A
featured_reviews.review_text:
Our experience was an 80–20 mix, but overall quite memorable. We’ve visited multiple restaurants across Mumbai and often seen chefs deeply occupied with their cooking schedules. Here, however, we met Chef Kunal Nagpal—a chef with a story, beautifully balancing restaurant management and creating magic with his food.

We reached the hotel around 3:45 PM, just before closing time, which meant our order was taken in a bit of a hurry. We patiently waited for the food, and that’s where the experience truly took a turn for the better.

We ordered Chicken Malai Tikka and Butter Chicken, and both dishes were outstanding. The masala was rich and delicious. A special recommendation: do try their Chicken Malai Tikka—it’s a must!

Overall rating: 8/10. If you’re a fan of Mughlai chicken, this restaurant is definitely worth a visit.

Chef, we wish you continued success and all the best for your future endeavours.

Thank you,
Sagar & Tejashree

featured_reviews.name: Chanjeet Dhawan
featured_reviews.review_text:
If you are looking for that authentic Mumbai seafood vibe, Jai Jawan in Bandra is pure bliss. Here is a breakdown of a legendary meal:

The Star: Fried Fish with Pav

The Fried Fish here is iconic—perfectly seasoned, crispy on the outside, and flaky within. But the real game-changer is pairing it with the Mumbai Pav. There is something about the texture and flavor of a local Mumbai pav that just hits differently; it’s the ultimate vessel for the spicy fish, especially when you load it up with their signature green chutney and crunchy onions. It’s a simple combination, but it's a "Mumbaikar" soul-food experience

The Sides & Mains
• Prawns Crispy: These lived up to the name. Golden, crunchy, and packed with flavor, they are the perfect appetizer to snack on while you soak in the Bandra energy

• Chicken Tawa Biryani: To wrap things up, the Chicken Tawa Biryani is a must-try. Unlike traditional dum biryanis, the tawa style gives it a unique, rustic smoky flavor and a spice profile that is bold and satisfying.

The Verdict
Eating here isn't just about the food; it's about the "Bliss of Taste." If you want to eat like a true Mumbaikar, grabbing a plate of fish and pav at Jai Jawan is an absolute rite of passage.

Highly Recommended for: Seafood lovers and anyone craving an authentic taste of Mumbai’s street-side culinary excellence.

Small sitting but service is super fast and turn around table is that like always waiting customers in big rush.

All the best team JJ.

Regards!
CSD

featured_reviews.name: Prakash Dhalwani
featured_reviews.review_text:
Jai Jawan never disappoints! Tried the butter chicken, fish tikka, paneer makhanwala, roti and naan — and every dish was a winner.

The butter chicken was absolutely amazing — full of flavour with the perfect spice level. The paneer makhanwala was equally impressive, with the softest paneer I've had in a while. But the real standout was the fish tikka — completely boneless and one of the best tikkas I've ever tasted!

A few things to keep in mind before you visit: there's no parking in the area, so plan your commute accordingly. They have both AC and non-AC seating, and during peak hours you may wait up to 15–20 mins for a table — but honestly, the food is well worth it!

Highly recommend for anyone craving authentic Indian flavours. Will definitely be back! 🙌

featured_reviews.name: Pinkesh Kamwani

Jai Jawan has been one of my favourite places in Bandra for years, and it continues to deliver every single time.

The Prawns Punjabi Fry is an absolute standout — juicy, flavourful, and cooked perfectly. It’s one of those dishes that keeps bringing you back.

The Seekh Kebabs have been consistently top-notch for over two decades, which is a testament to the kitchen’s consistency and quality.

And then comes the Butter Chicken — rich, indulgent, and simply outstanding. Easily among the best I’ve had.

What I appreciate most is that despite its popularity over the years, the food quality has remained remarkably consistent.

For me, it’s hard to think of a better place in Bandra for non-vegetarian food. If you’re a meat lover, Jai Jawan is a place you simply shouldn’t miss. 👍🍗🦐🔥

featured_reviews.name: Vinayak Londhe
featured_reviews.review_text:
Jai Jawan, Bandra

I recently visited Jai Jawan with my friends after a movie, mainly because we had seen and heard a lot about the place through Instagram reels. Since we were already in Bandra, we decided to give it a try. We reached the restaurant around 9:00 PM, which is peak dinner time, and had to wait for nearly 20 minutes to get a table for four—which was understandable considering the rush.

Once seated, we ordered Chicken Tikka Masala and Chicken Tandoori as starters. The starters were okayish in taste, nothing impressive. I assume this might have been due to the restaurant working at full capacity during peak hours.

For the main course, we ordered Butter Chicken with Rumali Rotis. Unfortunately, this was the biggest disappointment of the night. I’ve had butter chicken at countless restaurants, and honestly, this was the worst butter chicken I’ve had so far—lacking flavor, richness, and balance. We also ordered Chicken Fried Rice, which again was just average.

The service experience further added to the disappointment. There was a shortage of waiters, resulting in long waiting times for food. The staff seemed extremely busy and didn’t really have the time to listen properly to customer requests or feedback.

Another thing that stood out negatively was the entertainment setup. The restaurant has two large TV screens, but they were continuously playing the same 5-minute loop video of a Japanese city. On that particular day, there was an India cricket match, and playing it on at least one screen would have kept customers engaged—especially since food service was delayed.

Overall, I personally regret choosing Jai Jawan that night and feel I could have had a better experience elsewhere. This is purely my personal opinion. You may still try it once to form your own view, but my experience was not a good one.

featured_reviews.name: Dharmesh Dulera
featured_reviews.review_text:
The freshness of the seafood here is immediately evident. Every dish feels like it has come straight from the ocean to your plate, bursting with natural flavor. The fish is perfectly cooked—tender, juicy, and never overdone—while the prawns are plump, succulent, and seasoned to perfection. Their signature preparations strike a beautiful balance between bold coastal spices and authentic home-style cooking, making each bite deeply satisfying.

What truly sets Jai Jawan apart is its consistency and authenticity. There’s no unnecessary fuss or overcomplication—just honest, well-executed dishes that showcase the richness of Mumbai’s coastal cuisine. The masalas are aromatic without being overpowering, allowing the seafood to remain the star of the show.

The service is quick, efficient, and warm, adding to the overall comfort of the dining experience. It’s the kind of place where you can relax, dig in, and leave completely content.

Whether you’re a hardcore seafood lover or simply looking to explore Mumbai’s culinary treasures, Jai Jawan is a must-visit. It’s not just a meal—it’s a celebration of fresh flavors, tradition, and the simple joy of eating great food.

featured_reviews.name: Piyush Aggarwal
featured_reviews.review_text:
As a long-time patron of Taj Lands End, I was disappointed by our recent lunch at Masala Bay. What was intended as a premium business catch-up resulted in a sub-par meal that did not reflect Taj’s usual excellence.

The Critique:
• Starters: The Prawns Lasunia were tough and difficult to cut, while the Chicken Angari lacked any distinct character.
• Mains: The Dhabewala Chicken felt uninspired—poorly marinated with a sauce-heavy base—and the Dhaniya Murgh was overcompensated with spice and oil rather than balanced flavor.
• Value: At a price point of ₹8,500, the culinary execution felt significantly below industry standards.

The Silver Lining:
The service staff and management were exceptionally attentive and clearly concerned by our feedback. While the hospitality remains world-class, the kitchen requires immediate attention to its consistency and flavor profiles. We left feeling the meal was unfortunately "criminal" for the price paid.

featured_reviews.review_text:
The Tanjore Tiffin Room is one of the finest places in the city to enjoy authentic South Indian cuisine in a refined yet welcoming setting. From the moment you enter, the ambience sets the tone — warm, classy, and thoughtfully designed with a blend of traditional and contemporary elements. It strikes the perfect balance between being vibrant and cosy, making it ideal for both family meals and relaxed dining with friends.

The food is truly the star here. Every dish is crafted with rich, traditional flavours that reflect the culinary heritage of South India. The tasting platter is a must-try, offering a wonderful selection of signature items that allow you to sample a variety of dishes in one go. Whether it’s the dosas, curries, or starters, everything is cooked to perfection and beautifully presented. The flavours are authentic without being overly spicy, appealing to a wide range of palates.

The service is excellent, with staff who are attentive, polite, and well-informed about the menu. Their recommendations are spot-on, and they ensure you’re comfortable throughout your visit. Another convenience is the availability of valet parking, which makes dining here hassle-free, especially during busy hours.

Overall, The Tanjore Tiffin Room delivers a delightful South Indian dining experience with great food, superb service, and charming ambience. Highly recommended.

featured_reviews.name: vishal sawant
featured_reviews.review_text:
Recently, I had the pleasure of dining at Hoppumm, a cozy Sri Lankan restaurant tucked away in Khar West.

The moment we stepped in, we were greeted with a warm and lively ambiance – minimalist yet vibrant decor that instantly transported us to the streets of Shrilanka.

Ambiance and Setting:
The interiors are stylish yet casual, perfect for a relaxed evening. Beautifully painted walls, masks hanged on the wall and subtle lighting created an inviting atmosphere.

Service:
The service was quick, efficient, and polite. Special thanks to Mr. Imran for his wonderful hospitality — he patiently introduced us to the different dishes and ensured prompt service throughout the evening, making our experience even more memorable.

Food Quality:
We tried a variety of dishes:

Pineapple & Basil Cooler (refreshing and balanced)

Kokum Sharbat (perfectly tangy and cooling)

Chicken & Cheese Kottu (a hearty, flavorful dish and is a MUST TRY)

Lankan Stewed Chilli Chicken (rich coconut broth with tender chicken)

Green Mango Chicken Curry (tangy, creamy curry served in a portion fit for one person)

Traditional Hopper (light and crispy, served along with Podi)

Hot Butter Squid (crispy yet juicy with a burst of flavors)

Lemony Chicken Delight Combo (the showstopper with a perfect balance of zest and spice. There were many different dishes added to rice including a fried chicken leg piece)

They also offered three different types of chatneys from spicy to sweet flavour and you can add according to your need.
Food wasn't much spicy.

Each dish was authentic, beautifully presented, and packed with bold flavors true to Sri Lankan cuisine. Portion sizes were quite satisfying for the price.

Hoppumm is a hidden gem for those looking to explore Sri Lankan cuisine in Mumbai.

featured_reviews.name: Suyash Karangutkar
featured_reviews.review_text:
We recently visited Hoppum, a true haven for authentic Sri Lankan cuisine, and it was quite the culinary journey!

We began with the Lankan Stewed Chilli Chicken, where tender chicken was stuffed into green chillies — a brilliant fusion of juicy meat, aromatic spices, and bold chilli heat. It set the tone for what we hoped would be an exciting meal.

The Chicken and Cheese Kottu followed, a popular Sri Lankan street dish featuring finely chopped roti tossed with vegetables and chicken. It was delicious, evoking nostalgic Indian chaat vibes (think ragda pattice) with its hearty and comforting flavors.

The Green Mango Chicken Curry was a standout — silky smooth, subtly tangy with green mango, and enriched with coconut. Paired with their traditional Hopper (similar to an appam), it was an absolute treat.

We also tried the Hot Butter Squid, which was flavorful and perfectly chewy — a must for seafood enthusiasts.

Portion sizes for starters felt on the smaller side, especially considering the price point. Another important thing to note was the food was pre-prepared, and simply heated and served.

To beat the heat, the bottled Pineapple & Basil Cooler and Kokum Sherbet provided much-needed refreshment.

Our meal wrapped up with the Lemony Chicken Delight Combo Rice, served beautifully in a banana leaf with rice, chicken leg, coconut chutneys, and garnishes. Unfortunately, while visually appealing, it lacked the bold flavors we anticipated and felt a bit bland.

While the restaurant greets you with a pleasant, warm ambiance, the seating feels quite congested. The small tables and pocket-café vibe were a bit of a letdown, especially for a place that serves such vibrant cuisine.

The owners and employees seem to have no respect for customers. Orders are handled carelessly, staff members are inattentive, and the overall attitude is arrogant and dismissive. Instead of making guests feel comfortable, they make you feel like a burden.

featured_reviews.name: Travel Foodie
featured_reviews.review_text:
Stepping into Royal Carriage feels like boarding a luxurious train from a bygone era — the interiors are stunning, and the train-themed setup adds a unique charm.

I started with the crispy corn and pepper and veg seekh kebabs — both were flavorful, well-spiced, and cooked to perfection. They’ve recently launched a chat counter, and I couldn’t resist trying the sev puri and bhel puri; they were fresh, tangy, and a delight for street-food lovers.

For dessert, the caramel custard was smooth and creamy, hitting just the right sweetness. On the drinks front, the watermelon mojito was refreshing and light, while the blue lagoon added a vibrant, citrusy twist to my mocktail experience.

The service was prompt, and the staff were courteous. A perfect place for a fun meal with friends or a unique dining experience in Bandra West. Will definitely come back to try more from their menu.

featured_reviews.name: Appetites India
featured_reviews.review_text:

We started with the Dragon Chicken it was crispy, spicy, and packed with that perfect Chinese flavor. The Malabari Prawns were juicy, well-marinated served with a tasty green chutney.

In mains we had The Royal Special Chicken it had two types of gravies and was full of rich, bold flavors. The Korean Pot Rice was a hit.
For drinks, we tried the Shirley Temple and Fruit Punch  both refreshing and cool.

Lastly we ended with  Caramel Custard creamy, and just the right amount of sweet.
